key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on connections, rather than using devices only as scalar weights, lets analogue neural networks efficiently model smooth continuous targets.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable ultra-low-power hardware for continuous control and other regression-style tasks, with a projected CMOS power near 30 microwatts.
method: Implement trainable nonlinear connection functions inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
Realize the nonlinear functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays
Transfer trained models to hardware and also simulate a memristive version to check device-agnostic behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved parameter efficiency for smooth tasks such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with quantified transfer fidelity across about 35,000 connections.
watch_item: The benefit is task-dependent and does not improve parameter efficiency for classification-like decision boundaries, so it may not help all workloads.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
